chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me: 'O Zayd! Be patient with the enemies of the favours, for you will not recompense the one who disobeys Allah regarding you with anything better than obeying Allah regarding him. O Zayd! Indeed Allah chose Islam and selected it, so be good companions of it with generosity and good character.'

key_terms.أَعْدَاءِ النِّعَمِ: enemies of the favours (those who receive kindness but act as enemies)

ai.seo_question: How should one respond to ungrateful people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Zayd al-Shahham to exercise patience (sabr) towards those who are ungrateful for the blessings bestowed upon them, framing the optimal response to their ingratitude as obedience to Allah in one's conduct towards them. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on internalizing divine pleasure through moral excellence (husn al-khuluq) and generosity (sakha), transforming social friction into spiritual elevation. The advice highlights that true victory over enemies lies not in retaliation but in aligning one’s actions with Allah’s will, thereby maintaining spiritual integrity amidst social trials.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahham,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said to me: ‘O Zayd! Observe patience upon the enemies of the favours, for you will never suffice yourself from the one who disobeys Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding you with anything more superior than your obedience to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding him. O Zayd! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Chose Al-Islam and Selected it, therefore be good companions of it by the generosity and the best manners’.
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’ alia ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr from abu ‘Usama Zayd al-Shahham from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once the Imam said to me, ‘O Zayd be patient against the enemies of the bounties (jealous people). You cannot compensate (retaliate to offset your suffering) from one who disobeys Allah through causing you to suffer, in other ways more properly, than obeying Allah in his case (in not causing any suffering to him). O Zayd Allah has chosen Islam and has selected it. Be good companions of Islam through generosity and excellence in moral behavior.’”
